subject: science
passage: Date palms in Khairpur District, in Pakistan's Sindh province, are traditionally watered by flooding the ground around each tree with canal water. Drip irrigation, which delivers water slowly through tubes to each tree's roots, is more expensive to install. Agricultural engineer Sana Soomro compared the two methods on neighboring plots of the same date variety for three seasons. She concluded that drip irrigation used far less water without reducing the harvest: ______

data.title: Water Use and Date Harvest under Two Irrigation Methods, per Tree

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

choices.A: drip-irrigated trees used about 4,000 liters of water per season, less than half the amount used by flooded trees.
choices.B: flooded trees produced about 10,000 kilograms of fruit per tree each season, more than drip-irrigated trees did.
choices.C: drip-irrigated trees used less than half as much water as flooded trees each season, yet produced about the same amount of fruit, 70 to 74 kilograms per tree.
choices.D: drip-irrigated trees produced dates that sold for a higher price at market than those from flooded trees.

explanation.why: Soomro's conclusion has two parts: far less water and no loss of harvest. The support must use both the water and the fruit columns. Drip trees used 4,000 to 4,300 liters against 9,600 to 10,300 for flood trees, and their fruit (74, 70, 73 kilograms) was within a couple of kilograms of the flood trees' (72, 68, 75).
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is accurate, but it covers only the water saving and never mentions the harvest, so it cannot show that yields were unaffected.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This misreads the table: about 10,000 is the number of liters of water a flooded tree used, not kilograms of fruit; the fruit figures are 68 to 75 kilograms.
explanation.C: Correct. This pairs the large water saving with nearly identical harvests, supporting both halves of the conclusion.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The table says nothing about prices.
